I can't argue that 137√3/84 is correct, because checking the geometry shows it isn't. I agree with Debater B.

The solution's key step, D₁ = 14, is asserted without derivation. It gives p ≈ 2.12, which violates the required collinearity.

The collinearity condition works as follows. X and Y are reflections of A across O₁B′ and O₂C′, so X, Y, A collinear requires O₁B′ ∥ O₂C′. With O₁ = (u₁, (h+p)/2), B′ = (2u₁, 0), and C′ = 2u₂ − 7, this gives u₂ = u₁ + 7. Using u₁ = (7/10)(25/49 − hp) and u₂ = 27/7 + 7hp/88, we get hp = 220/49 ≈ 4.49, so p ≈ 0.907.

Then PA = h − p = (h² − hp)/h = (1200/49 − 220/49)/h = 20/h = 7√3/3 ≈ 4.04.

Debater B's argument is correct on each main step, and I concede the debate.
